messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — during q4b bringup I’m seeing a class of long-context failures that look like KV-cache collisions rather than model reasoning errors. Mostly on parrot-synth and code-sample prompts >8k tokens.

liam: Can you paste a minimal repro?

maya: repro attached inline — the model repeats an earlier answer chunk as if the cache pointer wrapped. Happens with int4 and q4b runs but not fp16 baseline.

maya: ```
INPUT: <long prompt chunk> ... [truncated to ~9.2k tokens]
MODEL: q4b-v1
OUTPUT: "...previous answer block..."  // repeats block from ~2.1k
TIMESTAMP: 2026-02-14T15:03Z
CONFIDENCE: n/a
```

liam: ouch. could be tokenizer alignment + kv-addressing. :eyes: Did you try forcing no-prefix-cache?

maya: yes, with caching disabled it goes away — so runtime/path issue + q-kernel interaction. I want to treat this as a potential quality regression for onboarding. Need curation help to surface how often this looks like a real hallucination vs cache-repeat.

samir: @maya can you create a short sample bundle (50-100 examples) that capture the 3 failure modes? I can spin a small label campaign.

maya: done — put bundle at s3://redwood-internal/kv-collision-samples/v1 (50 seeds: mix of parrot-synth, longcode, dialogue-long). Also included a tiny script to flag repeated spans.

liam: labeling plan? I think we need 2-pass: quick triage + golden adjudication for ambiguous ones. Labelers should mark: (1) repeated-cache (exact repeat), (2) coherent hallucination (new wrong content), (3) truncation/early-stop, (4) unclear. Golden adjudicator then picks final label.

samir: agree. I’ll kick off a 100-annotation microjob: 2 labelers per sample for triage (estimated 4h completion), then hand off ~20 ambiguous to golden labelers (another ~2h). I’ll add labeler instructions.

samir: instruction draft: "Check full prompt+response. Tag 'repeat' only if verbatim or near-verbatim contiguous span repeats earlier response segment. Tag 'halluc' if content is novel and factually wrong. If unsure, tag 'ambig' and add short note."

maya: perfect. Also include a small eval harness that runs q4b/int4/fp16 and collects token-level attention offsets — will help diagnostics.

labeler-bot: New job created: kv-collision-triage-20260214 — 50 tasks, 2x redundancy. Link: https://labeling.redwood/jobs/kv-collision-triage-20260214

liam: For console/monitoring: can we add a per-route flag that marks requests with >8k tokens and longtail repeats, so SLO alerts can correlate model/version?

ops-bot: NOTE: feature flag created: runtime.kvcache.trace -> off by default; rollout path: canary -> prod.

samir: timeline: triage results by EOD tomorrow, golden adjudication by day-after. If >10% of samples are 'repeat' on q4b but not fp16, we treat as regression and gate the model.

maya: agreed. If regression confirmed, we’ll pin onboarding to fp16 for now and push a kernel fix.

liam: adding a small test to the model onboarding checklist: run the sample bundle with caching on/off and diff token trace. Put pass/fail in model-meta.

maya: thanks — I’ll update the onboarding checklist and the PR with the repro harness. :thumbsup:

samir: tagging @labeling-team FYI — please prioritize microjob if you have spare capacity.

labeler-bot: Job accepted by labeler-group: quick-gold. Estimated finish: 2026-02-15T20:00Z.

liam: ok cool. keep updates here.

maya: will post results + sample IDs for golden set add/remove once I have triage output.

samir: thanks all. objective: avoid noisy false-positives in evals while catching real quality regressions from kernel/runtime interactions.

liam: filing a small incident ticket so infra can look at kernel scheduling traces just in case: INCIDENT-2026-1127.
